title: Family and "my, your"
why: The possessives שֶׁלִּי, שֶׁלְּךָ, שֶׁלָּךְ… are built on the same endings as לִי, לְךָ, which you saw in the previous lesson. You also learn the family words so you can introduce your own family.

Whose? שֶׁל

שֶׁל means \"of,\" in the sense of belonging: הַכֶּלֶב שֶׁל נֹעָה (Noa's dog, literally \"the dog of Noa\"). To ask whose something is: שֶׁל מִי זֶה? (whose is it?)

With pronouns, שֶׁל takes the same endings as the לִי, לְךָ, לָךְ… you've just learned:

HebrewPronunciationMeaning
שֶׁלִּיshelimy, mine
שֶׁלְּךָshelkhayour, yours (to a man)
שֶׁלָּךְshelakhyour, yours (to a woman)
שֶׁלּוֹshelohis
שֶׁלָּהּshelaher, hers
שֶׁלָּנוּshelanuour, ours
שֶׁלָּכֶםshelakhemyour, plural (men or a mixed group)
שֶׁלָּכֶןshelakhenyour, plural (women)
שֶׁלָּהֶםshelahemtheir (m.)
שֶׁלָּהֶןshelahentheir (f.)
שֶׁל מִי זֶה? זֶה שֶׁלִּי.Whose is this? It's mine. [shel mi ze? ze sheli]

\"My house\": the house of mine

The possessive goes after the noun, and the noun takes the article הַ: הַבַּיִת שֶׁלִּי, literally \"the house of mine.\" Without the article, בַּיִת שֶׁלִּי would rather mean \"a house of mine.\"

הַבַּיִת שֶׁלִּי גָּדוֹל.My house is big. [ha-bayit sheli gadol]

The good news: two things work just like English:

  • שֶׁלִּי doesn't change with the object, just like \"my\": הַבַּיִת שֶׁלִּי (my house), הַדִּירָה שֶׁלִּי (my apartment), הַיְלָדִים שֶׁלִּי (my children).
  • \"His\" and \"her\" depend on the owner, not on the object: הַבַּיִת שֶׁלּוֹ (his house), הַבַּיִת שֶׁלָּהּ (her house). Exactly as in English.

With אַבָּא and אִמָּא, Israelis often drop the article: אַבָּא שֶׁלִּי, אִמָּא שֶׁלִּי. Both are fine.

סָבָאסַבְתָּאgrandfather / grandmother [saba / savta]
דּוֹדדּוֹדָהuncle / aunt [dod / doda]
בֵּןבַּתson / daughter [ben / bat]
יֶלֶדיַלְדָּהboy / girl, child [yeled / yalda]
בַּעַלאִשָּׁהhusband / wife [ba'al / isha]

הוֹרִים (horim): parents; יְלָדִים (yeladim): children; מִשְׁפָּחָה (mishpakha): family. אִשָּׁה means both \"woman\" and \"wife.\"

הָאָחוֹת שֶׁלִּי גָּרָה בְּחֵיפָה עִם הַבַּעַל שֶׁלָּהּ.My sister lives in Haifa with her husband. [ha-akhot sheli gara be-Kheifa im ha-ba'al shela]

Before א, the article becomes הָ: הָאָח, הָאָחוֹת, הָאִשָּׁה.
